behaviors.behavior: Apply dismantle on a loop to unroll that loop and all its outer loops and specialize them with the given sparsity attribute.
behaviors.precondition: dismantle is applied on a loop; a sparsity attribute is given.

evidence.quote: When dismantle is applied on a loop, this loop and all its outer loops are unrolled and specialized with the given sparsity attribute.

behaviors.behavior: Jointly perform loop unrolling and dead code elimination (DCE) via dismantle.
behaviors.precondition: dismantle is applied to a loop nest.

evidence.quote: we introduce a new schedule primitive dismantle that jointly performs loop unrolling and DCE.

behaviors.behavior: Eliminate dead computation runs of the loop body within level l according to the sparsity pattern.
behaviors.precondition: dismantle has unrolled the loop and its outer loops; the pruning sparsity attribute is specified at block-size granularity; the loop body at level l aligns with the block size; unrolled body instances correspond to pruned blocks.

evidence.quote: many runs of the loop body within level l are dead computation
According to the sparsity pattern in Figure 7(a), six of them are dead computation and can be eliminated.

behaviors.behavior: Embed a specific sparsity pattern into the code, eliminating the need for sparsity encoding such as CSR.
behaviors.precondition: dismantle specializes code with a given sparsity attribute.

evidence.quote: dismantle embeds a specific sparsity pattern into the code, which eliminates the need of sparsity encoding, e.g., compressed sparse row (CSR)

behaviors.behavior: Remove indirect addressing overhead on the index because indices to non-pruned blocks/elements are specialized in the code.
behaviors.precondition: The index to non-pruned blocks/elements is specialized in the code.

evidence.quote: the overhead of indirect addressing on the index is removed

behaviors.behavior: Produce differently specialized code when given a different transformation plan and specialization hints (e.g., a smaller block size yields a smaller loop-body Matmul and more DCEs).
behaviors.precondition: A different transformation plan and corresponding specialization hints are provided.

evidence.quote: Given a different transformation plan (and the specification hints), the code can be specialized differently.
The hint in Figure 7(c) show a smaller block size. In this case, the loop body is a smaller Matmul (i.e., [2,1]x[1,1]), which enables more DCEs.

behaviors.behavior: Directly specialize a single value of W into the code without maintaining a sparse tensor W in memory when the small Matmul accesses only that one value.
behaviors.precondition: The chosen block size makes the loop body access a single value of W.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, as the small Matmul only accesses one value in W, the value can be directly specialized to the code (i.e., Wx,y) without maintaining a sparse tensor W in memory.

behaviors.behavior: Fall back to existing general sparse kernels (cuSPARSE, taco) or a dense kernel if it performs better when a specialization hint specifies block size equal to the tensor's shape.
behaviors.precondition: Specialization hint specifies block size equal to the whole tensor shape (one block covers the whole tensor).
search_terms: block size equal to tensor shape

evidence.quote: A specialization hint could also specify the block size equal to the tensor’s shape (i.e., one block covers the whole tensor). In this case, SparTA can directly use the existing state-of-the-art general sparse kernel implementation (e.g., cuSPARSE [3], taco [53]) or even use the dense kernel implementation if it perform better.

behaviors.behavior: Incorporate any sparsity-aware technique, including off-the-shelf sparse kernels and their dense versions, into the specialization framework.
behaviors.precondition: A sparsity-aware technique/kernel is available to be incorporated.

evidence.quote: SparTA’s specialization framework is general to incorporate any sparsity-aware techniques, including the off-the-shelf sparse kernel and even its dense version.

behaviors.behavior: Search from the outermost loop until the level l where the inner loop body aligns with the block size, then apply dismantle at that loop level.
behaviors.precondition: Specialization starts from a dense multi-level loop nest and a block size is given in the specialization hints.
search_terms: inner loop body aligns with block size

evidence.quote: It searches from the outermost loop until the level (say l) of inner loop body aligns with the block size.
dismantle is applied on the third loop, thus the top three loops are unrolled, generating eight small Matmuls (i.e., [2,2]x[2,2]).
